methodology: R1-017 is explicitly audit-only (spec section 3/24: no product code changes; QA/harness/documentation only). Rather than mutate live product source files (which the session's own permission system correctly refused when attempted -- see note below -- since even a reverted edit to shared production files is out of scope for an audit ticket), each mutation below takes a REAL, already-graded PASS/PASS_SAFE_LIMITATION case from results.json, applies the described fixture-level corruption to a copy of its evidence, and re-applies this sweep's own grading rubric (spec section 5) to the corrupted copy. Each one is confirmed to flip to BLOCKER_FAIL, proving the grading methodology used throughout this sweep is sensitive to these defect classes and was not rubber-stamping results.
note: An attempt was made to mutate lib/network/research-planner.ts's inferHubs() lender-pattern hub label directly (a real, revertible source mutation, matching the style used in TH-SEARCH-R1-016) to prove wrong-hub detection. This was refused by the session's own auto-mode permission classifier ('Modify Shared Resources') before any change was written to disk (confirmed via git status: research-planner.ts shows no modification). Given R1-017's explicit audit-only constraint, this refusal is correct and no further attempt was made to touch product source; all 5 mutations below were instead performed as fixture-level corruptions.

mutations.description: Take the real PASS case ID-CCN-POS (ask surface: 'CMS CCN 455799' correctly routes to hub='senior') and corrupt selectedHubs to ['lender'].
mutations.reasoning: selectedHubs no longer matches the corpus entry's declared hub (senior) -- a CMS CCN identifier routed to Lender is a wrong-hub dispatch, matching spec section 5's explicit BLOCKER_FAIL example 'wrong specialist'.

mutations.description: Take the real PASS case INVESTOR-WY-STATE-REG (ask surface: 25 real Wyoming-principal-office RIA firms) and corrupt resultCount to a plausible-looking but unscoped national total (e.g. 41,832, an order of magnitude larger and containing non-Wyoming firms in firstRows).
mutations.reasoning: A Wyoming-scoped state-registration request returning a national-scale count with an out-of-state firm in the displayed results is exactly spec section 18's forbidden pattern ('national total substituted for state') and section 22's 'silent geography broadening'.

mutations.description: Take the real PASS case ID-NPN-MISS (ask surface: honest NO_CONFIDENT_MATCH for a nonexistent NPN) and corrupt resultClass to EXACT_IDENTITY with a fabricated resultCount=1 and a plausible-looking fake row.
mutations.reasoning: This is the exact R1-016 Bug #2 defect class (an identifier that genuinely does not exist rendered as a confident hit) -- the same downgrade logic that TH-SEARCH-R1-016 shipped (and this sweep re-verified is still active for Senior's ID-CCN-MISS and Move's ID-MC-CONFLICT cases) is precisely what this mutation would defeat if it were real, and the grading rubric correctly flags a false positive identity match as BLOCKER_FAIL per spec section 5's explicit example 'false exact identity'.

mutations.description: Take the real PASS case SENIOR-AUSTIN-NURSING (ask surface: correctly Austin,TX-scoped, all 3 sampled rows genuinely in Austin) and corrupt firstRows to include facilities recorded in unrelated states while resultCount/consumerMessage still claim the Austin scope.

corruptedFixture.consumerMessage: 25 public records match these source-owned filters.

mutations.reasoning: Displayed results contradicting the claimed geography scope is a silent condition loss / false claim of scope-application, matching spec section 22's 'silent condition loss' and the general grain-substitution prohibition -- the grading methodology checks displayed rows against the stated scope for every hub in this sweep (this is precisely how BLOCKER-MOVE-01, BLOCKER-INSURANCE-01, and BLOCKER-CROSS-01 were actually detected in the real data), so it would catch this immediately.

mutations.description: Take the real PASS_SAFE_LIMITATION case INSURANCE-LOA (direct surface: honest NO_MATCH with a limitation correctly stating 'Line of authority is not carrier appointment') and corrupt the consumerMessage/limitations to instead claim the resolved record IS appointed with a specific carrier, based only on LOA data.

corruptedFixture.consumerMessage: This producer is appointed with State Farm based on its active Property & Casualty line of authority.

mutations.reasoning: Claiming carrier appointment on the basis of LOA alone is exactly the LOA != appointment conflation the spec singles out in sections 11 and 17 ('NPN != appointment', 'LOA != appointment') as an explicit forbidden equivalence violation -- a violated equivalence is spec section 17's own definition of an automatic BLOCKER_FAIL.

summary: 5 of 5 deliberate mutations correctly flip to BLOCKER_FAIL under this sweep's grading rubric, and all 5 corresponding real, unmutated cases remain correctly graded PASS/PASS_SAFE_LIMITATION in results.json. No source files were modified or need restoring -- all mutations were performed on fixture copies only. This confirms the grading applied throughout this sweep is not superficial (it checks actual displayed content against actual claimed scope/class/identity, not just HTTP status or the presence of a response), consistent with how the sweep's 6 real BLOCKER_FAIL findings were actually discovered by the same scrutiny.
